assistant|endurance_cardio_recommendatio: Do cardio such as jogging, cycling, or swimming 20-30 minutes, 2-3 times a week for soccer endurance.
assistant|endurance_hiit_recommendation: Do HIIT: sprint 20-30 seconds then 1-2 minutes active recovery, repeated for 20-30 minutes.
assistant|endurance_hill_sprints_recomme: Sprint up a hill at maximum effort 20-30 seconds, recover on the way down, repeat 20-30 minutes.
assistant|endurance_small_sided_games: Play small-sided games like 3v3 or 4v4 with friends or teammates for game-like endurance.
assistant|recovery_sleep_recommendation: Aim for 7-9 hours of sleep and take rest days as needed for recovery.
get 7-9 hours of sleep each night for recovery
assistant|running_cadence_recommendation: Aim for a running cadence of 160-170 steps per minute with quick, light steps.
assistant|running_footstrike_recommendat: Land midfoot or forefoot instead of heel striking to reduce joint impact.
assistant|running_arm_swing_recommendati: Keep arms relaxed and bent around 90 degrees without crossing the body.
assistant|shooting_technique_recommendat: Lock the ankle with toes down, strike with laces or inside of foot, and follow through.
assistant|shooting_both_feet_recommendat: Practice shooting with both feet to become more unpredictable and versatile.
assistant|tournament_prep_timeline: Do physical and technical training 4-6 weeks before the tournament, mental prep 2-4 weeks out.
assistant|tournament_mental_prep: Set realistic tournament goals, visualize success, manage nerves, and analyze opponents.
visualize crossing the finish line in under 25:50 and use positive self-talk
visualize serving aces and winning games, use breathing and relaxation to reduce nerves, and develop a pre-serve routine
assistant|tournament_week_recommendation: During tournament week, taper training, prioritize recovery, and get familiar with the venue.
assistant|racket_choice_recommendation: Choose a racket based on swing style, skill level, weight and balance, and grip size.
assistant|string_choice_recommendation: Consider string type (synthetic vs natural gut), tension, pattern, gauge, and hybrid setups.
assistant|endurance_strength_training: Do strength training targeting legs, core, and glutes — squats, lunges, deadlifts, leg press — to build power and endurance.
do strength training 2-3 times a week with at least one rest day in between
assistant|endurance_plyometrics: Do plyometric exercises like jump squats, box jumps, and burpees to improve explosiveness and power.
assistant|agility_drills_recommendation: Incorporate agility drills like cone drills, ladder drills, and shuttle runs to improve speed, agility, and direction changes.
assistant|warmup_cooldown_recommendation: Warm up properly before games and cool down afterwards to prevent injuries and aid recovery.
warm up and cool down with a 10-minute easy run around interval workouts
warm up before strength training and cool down afterwards to prevent injury
assistant|hydration_nutrition_recommenda: Drink plenty of water and eat a balanced diet with complex carbohydrates, lean protein, and healthy fats.
assistant|gradual_progression_advice: Start slowly, gradually increase intensity and duration, and avoid overtraining to prevent injury or burnout.
assistant|running_posture_recommendation: Maintain a tall, upright posture while running, as if a string pulls your head toward the ceiling.
assistant|core_engagement_recommendation: Engage your core muscles while running to maintain good posture and generate power.
assistant|breathing_technique_recommenda: Practice rhythmic breathing, exhaling on one footstrike and inhaling on the other to stay relaxed.
assistant|running_with_ball_recommendati: Practice running with a soccer ball at your feet to control speed and direction while running.
assistant|soccer_change_of_direction: Practice quick changes of direction — cutting, weaving, decelerating — to navigate the soccer field efficiently.
assistant|soccer_pacing_advice: Pace yourself during a game: start at a moderate pace and adjust to the game's intensity.
assistant|soccer_arms_use_advice: Use your arms to shield the ball, create space, and protect yourself from opponents.
assistant|soccer_head_up_advice: Keep your head up and eyes forward during games to stay aware of surroundings and teammates.
assistant|soccer_game_situations_practic: Practice game scenarios like making runs, receiving passes, and creating scoring opportunities.
assistant|shooting_stance_recommendation: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, dominant foot forward, knees slightly bent, and back straight when shooting.
assistant|shooting_weight_transfer: Shift weight to the back foot, then transfer it to the front foot as you strike to generate power.
assistant|shooting_shot_types_practice: Practice different shot types — driven shots, finesse shots, and volleys — to adapt to game situations.
assistant|shooting_watch_professionals: Watch professional soccer players and study their stance, ball positioning, and striking technique.
assistant|shooting_pressure_practice: Practice shooting under game-like pressure with defenders closing in to build composure.
assistant|finishing_movement_positioning: Improve movement, timing, and positioning in the box to create space and scoring opportunities.
assistant|finishing_drills_recommendatio: Practice finishing drills — both feet, volleys, breakaways — to improve technique and confidence.
assistant|tournament_physical_training: Build cardio endurance, strength and power, agility, and on-court conditioning before the tournament.
assistant|tournament_technical_refinemen: Practice serves (flat, topspin, slice), footwork, forehand/backhand/volleys, and returns before the tournament.
assistant|racket_demo_advice: Demo and experiment with different rackets and strings; many tennis shops offer demo rackets and stringing.

assistant|strength_glutes_lunges: Lunges stepping forward and lowering body, pushing through front heel
assistant|strength_glutes_glute_bridges: Glute bridges lifting hips toward ceiling and squeezing glutes at top

assistant|strength_legs_step_ups: Step-ups onto a step or bench, one foot at a time

assistant|strength_feet_ankle_circles: Ankle circles drawing circles with the ankle, foot lifted off ground
assistant|strength_feet_single_leg_balan: Single-leg balance standing on one foot for 30 seconds to improve balance and stability
assistant|strength_rep_range: start with lower weights and higher reps (12-15) to focus on endurance
assistant|serve_grip: use Continental or Eastern Forehand grip for right-handers, Western Forehand grip for left-handers
assistant|serve_toss_height: toss about 6-8 feet in the air, slightly in front of body with a high arc

assistant|serve_power_generation: use legs and hips to generate power, transferring weight from back foot to front foot

assistant|toss_drill_visualize: Toss and Visualize: toss up, visualize ball going into the service box, then catch

assistant|speed_work_sprints: incorporate shorter, faster runs such as 200-400m sprints at high intensity to build speed and endurance

assistant|fuel_and_hydration: eat a balanced diet with complex carbohydrates, lean protein, and healthy fats; stay hydrated before, during, and after runs

assistant|hip_flexor_exercises: leg swings and side lunges target the hip flexors to improve running stride
